It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while considering the “noise and tumult” of a world where enemies of the Cross are often transformed into its most vocal defenders, and I must ask you with a gentle spirit: why do you ask after the conversion of those who once sought to destroy the faith? [11, 13, 28, 1381, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” who “do not spare the flock,” or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that “not one human sinner or demonic power will ever succeed in his rebellion” against the King? [13, 20, 283, 1143, 1221, 1408, 1425, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to offer “spiritual placebos” that ignore the necessity of a “supernatural work of God,” we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Master personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” by raising up “chosen vessels” from the ranks of His opponents [11, 28, 251, 1086, 1313, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the turning of a persecutor into a witness is not an “administrative anomaly” but is subject to the “decree from God” who “sovereignly orders everything He has made” [15, 68, 191, 1143, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Conversion of the Foremost Enemy**

**Verse**
“Then Saul, still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest and asked letters from him to the synagogues of Damascus, so that if he found any who were of the Way, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem. As he journeyed he came near Damascus, and suddenly a light shone around him from heaven. Then he fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to him, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?’ And he said, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ Then the Lord said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting. It is hard for you to kick against the goads’ ” (Acts 9:1–5). [113, 116, 127, 180, 245, 267, 1125, 1284, 1408, 1425, 1442, 1443, 1457, 1484, 1528, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur**—notes that Saul of Tarsus was a “savage wolf” who oversaw a “brutal campaign of terror” against the church [180, 1425, 1528, Conversation History]. His transformation was not a result of “human effort” or a “conscious choice” born of his own will, but was a “miracle of God” that occurred when he was “instantly and utterly transformed” by the resurrected Christ [11, 15, 138, 181, 220, 251, 621, 680, 1308, 1443, 1532, Conversation History]. The Lord Jesus identified Saul as a “chosen vessel” even while Saul was “breathing threats and murder,” proving that “salvation is a supernatural work” which God “initiates and accomplishes” according to His own “uninfluenced, free, electing choice” (Acts 9:15) [11, 251, 353, 356, 1086, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by a “no-lordship ideology” that suggests sinners “accept” Jesus on their own terms, for “unless the Father draws them,” no one can come to the Son [91, 356, 1308, 1406, 1502, Conversation History]. Recognize that “your life is not your own” because you were “bought at a price,” and if God could turn the “chief of sinners” into an apostle, He can “perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle” any soul according to His purpose (1 Timothy 1:15; 1 Peter 5:10) [12, 101, 858, 922, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, Saul was a “Pharisee, a son of Pharisees,” who believed his “ritualized ceremonies” and “zeal” made him “blameless” under the Law (Philippians 3:5–6) [180, 1313, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our standing, revealing that “by the deeds of the law no flesh will be justified,” for Saul eventually counted his “efforts to be righteous” as “rubbish” in order to gain the “righteousness which is from God by faith” (Romans 3:20; Philippians 3:8–9) [181, 234, 300, 1169, 1188, 1403, 1420, 1709, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: Providence in the Lives of Persecutors-Turned-Witnesses**

**Verse**
“And they stoned Stephen as he was calling on God and saying, ‘Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.’ Then he fell on his knees and cried out with a loud voice, ‘Lord, do not hold this sin against them.’ And when he had said this, he fell asleep” (Acts 7:59–60). [46, 69, 1060, 1075, 1221, 1284, 1340, 1426, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture reveals that God “harnesses the deeds of the wicked” to accomplish His “good purposes,” as seen when the “horrible pit” of Stephen’s martyrdom became the occasion for Saul’s eventual conversion [5, 11, 69, 133, 1143, 1440, 1546, Conversation History]. The “record of history” shows that while “hostile nations” and “savage wolves” rage, “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan,” and the “Word of God is not chained” even when His witnesses are (Psalm 2:1; 2 Timothy 2:9) [11, 21, 25, 94, 121, 1132, 1315, 1408, 1420, 1425, 1515, 1572, 1684, Conversation History]. Stephen’s prayer was an “eloquent testimony” to the “saving desire” of God, serving as a “textbook” for the church that “death is but a harmless shadow” because “the Lord knows how to deliver the godly” (2 Peter 2:9) [11, 47, 67, 116, 176, 213, 300, 844, 1136, 1143, 1408, 1450, 1515, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” recognizing that the “mighty hand of God” is at work even when you are “reduced to skin and bones” or facing “various trials” (Psalm 102:5; James 1:2) [21, 65, 94, 121, 201, 352, 915, 1132, 1408, 1515, 1572, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your mind” to look past “momentary, light affliction,” knowing that “God causes all things to work together for good” (Romans 8:28; 2 Corinthians 4:17) [11, 14, 101, 113, 116, 121, 152, 201, 814, 920, 1072, 1406, 1408, 1515, 1546, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of Witness**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “testifying in a dispute” required strict “safeguards” to establish “justice for all” (Deuteronomy 17:6) [330, 367, 1072, 1230, 1317, 1365, 1473, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “victory,” teaching that the “church militant” conquers not through “carnal weaponry” but “by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony,” meaning the death of a martyr is the “choice legacy” of the King (Revelation 12:11) [13, 14, 21, 32, 92, 743, 1313, 1402, 1414, 1491, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

### **Section 3: The Doctrine of Regeneration (The Miracle of Life)**

**Verse**
“ ‘Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.’ Nicodemus said to Him, ‘How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb and be born?’ Jesus answered, ‘Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. Do not marvel that I said to you, “You must be born again” ’ ” (John 3:3–7). [597, 598, 599, 600, 604, 873, 1206, 1314, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Voddie Baucham** and **Paul Washer**—teaches that the “unregenerate soul” is “dead in trespasses,” “alienated from God,” and “hostile in mind,” making it “unable to save itself” [11, 214, 215, 342, 343, 807, 808, 1403, 1410, Conversation History]. Regeneration is the “washing” by which the Spirit “imparts life to dead hearts,” a “wholesale transformation” that occurs “not by the will of the flesh... but of God” (John 1:13; Titus 3:5) [11, 13, 133, 163, 251, 355, 356, 596, 603, 615, 1503, Conversation History]. This “new birth” gives the sinner a “new heart” that no longer “relishes rebellion” but instead “yields unconditionally to Christ” [138, 145, 254, 601, 1318, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You must “confess your own utter spiritual poverty,” recognizing that “the gospel has nothing to say to people who are satisfied with their own righteousness” [11, 61, 153, 191, 233, 314, 345, 1169, 1403, Conversation History]. “Saturate and renew your mind” with the truth that “you were born again, not of corruptible seed but incorruptible,” for “He who began a good work in you will complete it” (Philippians 1:6; 1 Peter 1:23) [5, 101, 105, 116, 221, 399, 1406, 1408, 1503, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Forensic and Familial standing**
In the ancient **context**, “adoption” of slaves resulted in their “freedom” and “objective standing” as heirs [389, 390, 395, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “inheritance,” showing that regeneration leads to “justification” (a judicial declaration of righteousness) and “adoption” (placement into God’s family), whereby we cry out “Abba, Father!” (Romans 8:15) [14, 26, 315, 347, 348, 385, 387, 391, 404, 610, 611, 861, 880, 1089, 1179, 1254, 1514, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 313, 332, 361, 405, 414, 444, 591, 1138, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].
